message.content: Pandas belong to the order Carnivora, but they diverged from other carnivores early on. Their lineage split from the ursid (bear) family around 20–25 million years ago. Fossil evidence shows that the giant panda’s ancestors were omnivorous bears that gradually adapted to a bamboo‑based diet. By the Pleistocene, the modern giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) had evolved its distinctive black‑and‑white coat and specialized wrist bone that acts like a thumb for gripping bamboo. The red panda (Ailurus fulgens), while sharing the name, is not closely related; it belongs to its own family Ailuridae and diverged from other carnivores earlier, around 40 million years ago.
